UK public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants in 2023-24, a 62% increase from 2019-20 levels, according to data from Tussell. Despite expectations that consultant spending would decrease after the COVID pandemic, expenditure remains elevated above pre-pandemic levels.

The new Labour government under Keir Starmer faces significant challenges in meeting its goal to halve consultant spending during this parliament. Since taking power, nearly £650m in new consultant contracts have been awarded, including a £223m deal with KPMG to train civil servants over the next 15 months.

Labour peer Prem Sikka criticized the spending as "scandalous," arguing that there is a "cult of hiring consultants" and questioning their ability to provide meaningful value given their limited time within complex organizations.
